-----Original Message-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem cert rotation & DNS handoff for private endpoints

Alice —

Appreciate the context. Off the top, there are two pragmatic patterns we recommend depending on your security posture and ops preferences: 

Option A — Edge TLS termination (recommended for most customers):
- Terminate TLS at your DMZ/load-balancer (F5/HAProxy/NGINX) or our edge Envoy deployed in your DMZ.
- Use customer-managed certs (public or private CA). Redwood verifies CSR/signing policy during onboarding.
- Mutual TLS between edge and Redwood services (mTLS) using short-lived certs minted by Vault/ACME + a private CA.
- Split-horizon: public-facing FQDNs map to edge IPs; internal view resolves to internal load balancer for health checks.

Pros: clear separation of responsibilities, customer keeps cert private keys; faster renewal operations.
Cons: additional network config in DMZ and firewall rules to allow egress to Redwood control plane if you use our certificate automation.

Option B — Pass-through / end-to-end TLS to Redwood Private instances:
- TLS passthrough at the edge; Redwood terminates with customer-provided cert bundle.
- Requires secure transfer mechanism for cert material (SFTP to a hardened KMS-backed bucket or storage in HSM-managed Vault we can integrate).

Pros: Redwood manages termination and can provide consistent behavior across regions.
Cons: you must trust cert material transfer/storage practices; higher audit requirements.

Specific asks from us to proceed with an architecture review: 
- Which option do you prefer (A or B)?
- For Option A: will you run Envoy/nginx in the DMZ or use LB? We'll need the edge health-check endpoints and firewall egress CIDRs.
- For Option B: who will provision the cert bundle and what transfer mechanism do you allow?

I've attached a short configuration guide (redwood-onprem-tls-configuration.pdf) and would propose a 45-min call early next week to lock design. Markus and Dev will join for kernel-level and network sizing questions.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-onprem-tls-configuration.pdf (pdf)

On Mon, 30 Jun 2025 at 09:08 AM, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:

> Karthik / Alice —
> 
> A few technical clarifications from infra: 
> 
> 1) If you pick Option A and run Envoy in your DMZ, we recommend Envoy do TLS offload and then use mutual TLS to the worker fleet with certs signed by your internal CA (we can accept an intermediate CA signed for Redwood to mint worker certs).
> 2) For automated rotation, we integrate with HashiCorp Vault PKI or an ACME endpoint that supports DNS-01 for issuing short-lived certs. If you need HSM-backed signing, we can use your HSM via PKCS#11 or our HSM in a dedicated tenant (requires an SLA).
> 3) DNS: split-horizon is fine. Redwood needs a stable internal record for service discovery (SRV / A records) and a provisioned TTL policy. We can accept zone updates pushed to an api endpoint (signed) or you can grant read-only DNS server access for controlled updates.
> 4) Compliance note: for SOC2 evidence we'll need the cert handling playbook (who has access to private keys, rotation schedule, logs). If you choose Option B, please include transfer audit logs.
> 
> I'll paste a minimal Envoy config snippet in the follow-up if helpful.
> 
> -Markus
> Markus Klein
> Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

- I'll have NetOps schedule a maint window for opening the 443/8443 egress to Redwood control plane IP ranges (Tom will follow up).
- We'll provision an Envoy instance in the DMZ and provide a zone export that maps the external FQDN to your edge. See attached DNS export.
- For rotation: we will continue to issue certs from our internal CA; please confirm Redwood can validate via OCSP/CRL or accept an intermediate signed cert.

Can you send a short mutual action plan (tasks, owners, dates) and an operations contact for firewall changes?

Best,
Alice
